title: Excluded From the Artists' Guild, He Exhibited Anyway
standfirst: In the early 1940s, wartime Romania struck Iosif Iser from the professional body that let a painter work in the country. Three years later his ballerinas and harlequins were hanging in a Bucharest gallery regardless — one stretch in a life that ran from mocking the monarchy in caricature to being decorated, twice over, by the state that replaced it.

sections.heading: By 1930, Paris Had Already Replaced His Tatars With Dancers and Clowns
sections.body: Iosif Iser spent most of the 1920s and early 1930s based in Paris, and in that stretch the subjects that had made his name in Romania — Tatar women painted after years on the Dobrogean coast — gave ground to a different cast entirely: café society, circus performers, harlequins and dancers, the [same milieu Picasso was working through](https://www.rador.ro/2023/04/25/portret-65-de-ani-de-la-moartea-pictorului-iosif-iser/) at the same moment. This canvas, dated 1930, sits in the middle of that run. Accounts of Iser's ballerina paintings from these years single out a recurring choice: dancers caught [resting rather than performing](https://www.deltadunariinews.ro/iosif-iser-balerine-si-arlechini/), worn out between numbers rather than mid-motion — a deliberate departure from what Degas had done with the same subject decades earlier. The catalogue label attached to this picture is Expressionism, the tag that fits the thick, unmodulated lines of Iser's Munich student work. By his own documented chronology, though, he had spent the previous decade softening exactly that style into brighter colour and looser handling. The label describes the painter he had already stopped being by 1930.

sections.heading: The Name on the Canvas Wasn't the One He Was Born With
sections.body: He signed his pictures Iser, but he was born on 21 May 1881 as [Iosif Isidor Rubinsohn](https://adevarul.ro/stil-de-viata/cultura/povestea-lui-iosif-iser-pictorul-care-a-desenat-2529810.html), to a Jewish family. Exactly where is disputed. Wikipedia and a later profile in Adevărul both place the birth in Bucharest, with the family moving on to Ploiești afterward. A regional Argeș newspaper covering a 2023 museum acquisition instead calls him the [son of a baker from Boteni](https://evenimentulmuscelean.ro/2023/01/06/tarancuta-din-muscel-semnata-de-iosif-iser-din-boteni-ultima-achizitie-de-arta-a-muzeului-judetean-arges/), a village in Muscel county, and dates his roots there from birth. What isn't disputed is his primary schooling in Pitești, where he became friends with a classmate who grew up to be the poet [Ion Minulescu](https://adevarul.ro/stil-de-viata/cultura/povestea-lui-iosif-iser-pictorul-care-a-desenat-2529810.html), a friendship that lasted the rest of both men's lives. He finished secondary school in Ploiești in 1899, enrolled to study architecture in Munich that same year, and gave it up for the art academy within months.

sections.heading: He Spent His Twenties Turning the Monarchy Into a Joke
sections.body: Back in Bucharest, and then in Paris from 1908, Iser built his early reputation less as a painter than as a caricaturist — political drawings for the socialist papers Facla and the original Adevărul, most of them satirising the Romanian monarchy and its bourgeoisie. In Montmartre he was [frequenting the same circles](https://adevarul.ro/stil-de-viata/cultura/povestea-lui-iosif-iser-pictorul-care-a-desenat-2529810.html) as André Derain and absorbing what the Fauves were doing with colour. When he returned to Bucharest in 1909 he organised the country's first exhibition of modern art at the Romanian Athenaeum, hanging his own canvases beside Derain's. It landed badly: that 1909 show [disappointed Bucharest's conservative public](https://adevarul.ro/stil-de-viata/cultura/povestea-lui-iosif-iser-pictorul-care-a-desenat-2529810.html), unused to what he'd brought back. The caricatures fared better. The poet Tudor Arghezi later credited Iser's arrival with changing what caricature even looked like in Romania, moving it on from a [crude, poorly-drawn form](https://mnlr.ro/en/iosif-iser-un-caricaturist-maestru-al-penelului/) into something worth taking seriously as art.

sections.heading: Excluded From the Artists' Guild, He Exhibited Anyway
sections.body: None of that standing survived the 1940s intact. Under wartime rule, and because he was Jewish, Iser was [struck from the professional body](https://vatra-mcp.ro/artisti-si-patrimoniu/pictori-romani/bucuresti/iosif-iser-pictor-grafician/) of Romanian visual artists and cut off from the official support that came with belonging to it. He kept painting anyway — the same rural scenes, odalisques and theatrical figures he had always painted. Then, in the middle of that persecution, a 1943 Bucharest show titled "[Light and Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iosif_Iser)" hung his work next to Gheorghe Petrașcu's and Alexandru Ciucurencu's — two of the era's most established Romanian painters, exhibiting alongside a man the same government had just struck from its own professional register.

sections.heading: The Regime That Followed Gave Him Every Medal It Had
sections.body: The government that replaced Antonescu's was communist, and it treated Iser altogether differently. He received Romania's [Order of Cultural Merit](https://www.rador.ro/2023/04/25/portret-65-de-ani-de-la-moartea-pictorului-iosif-iser/) in 1947, the Order of Labour First Class in 1951, and in 1954 the title Artist of the People, one of the state's highest honours for a working artist. On 2 July 1955 he became a full member of the Romanian Academy — the institution whose most conservative wing had shrugged off his first Paris-inflected exhibition forty-six years before. A 1956 retrospective at Bucharest's [Sala Dalles showed 388](https://adevarul.ro/stil-de-viata/cultura/povestea-lui-iosif-iser-pictorul-care-a-desenat-2529810.html) of his works while he was still alive to see it. He died on 25 April 1958. His widow, the sculptor Désirée Sterian, later gave several hundred of his paintings to what became Bucharest's [Museum of Art Collections](https://vatra-mcp.ro/artisti-si-patrimoniu/pictori-romani/bucuresti/iosif-iser-pictor-grafician/) — the core of how most of his ballerinas, odalisques and Tatars survive to be seen today.
